record.evidence_quote: The lowest common multiple (LCM) of two numbers is the smallest number that is a multiple of both. For example, the first three common multiples of the numbers 4 and 6 are 12, 24 and 36. The number 12 is the smallest of these multiples.

record.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors.

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 12 \\
 \hline
 2 & 6 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$12=2 \times 2 \times 3$$

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 18 \\
 \hline
 3 & 9 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$18=2 \times 3 \times 3$$

Step 2: Identify all the prime factors that must be included in a common multiple.

Any multiple of 12 must contain: $2 \times 2$ (The factor $3$ is included in $3 \times3$; see next line)
Any multiple of 18 must contain: $3 \times 3$ (The factor $2$ is included in $2 \times 2$; see previous line)

A multiple that contains $2\times 2$ automatically contains $2$. Similarly, a multiple that contains $3\times 3$ automatically contains $3$.

Step 3: Multiply the prime factors that have to be included in both multiples to get the LCM.

$$\text{LCM} = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 = 36$$

 5 & 5 \\

$$45=3^2 \times 5$$

The factor 2 was used and its highest index is two: $2^2$
The factor 3 was used and its highest index is two: $3^2$

record.evidence_quote: ### Exercise 2.10: Use different methods to find the LCM 2. For the following sets of numbers, express each number as a product of prime factors and then find the LCM. 9 and 12 20 and 50 24 and 40 6, 8 and 12 10, 16 and 18
record.prompt_text:
### Exercise 2.10: Use different methods to find the LCM

2. For the following sets of numbers, express each number as a product of prime factors and then find the LCM.

9 and 12
20 and 50
24 and 40
6, 8 and 12
10, 16 and 18
record.answer_text:
9 and 12
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
3 & 9 \\
\hline
3 & 3 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$9=3 \times 3$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 12 \\
\hline
2 & 6 \\
\hline
3 & 3 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$12=2 \times 2 \times 3$$
Any multiple of 9 must contain: $3\times3$
Any multiple of 12 must contain: $2\times2$ ($3$ is included in $3\times3$)
$$\therefore \text{LCM} = 3 \times 3 \times 2 \times 2 = 36$$

20 and 50
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 20 \\
\hline
2 & 10 \\
\hline
5 & 5 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$20=2 \times 2 \times 5$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 50 \\
\hline
5 & 25 \\
\hline
5 & 5 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$50=2 \times 5 \times 5$$
Any multiple of 20 must contain: $2\times2$ ($5$ is included in $5\times5$ below)
Any multiple of 50 must contain: $5\times5$ ($2$ is included in $2\times2$ above)
$$\therefore \text{LCM} = 2 \times 2 \times 5 \times 5 = 100$$

24 and 40
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 24 \\
\hline
2 & 12 \\
\hline
2 & 6 \\
\hline
3 & 3 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$24=2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 40 \\
\hline
2 & 20 \\
\hline
2 & 10 \\
\hline
5 & 5 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$40=2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5$$
Any multiple of both 24 and 40 must contain: $2 \times 2 \times 2$
Any multiple of 24 must contain: $3$
Any multiple of 40 must contain: $5$
$$\therefore \text{LCM} = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 5 = 120$$

6, 8 and 12
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 6 \\
\hline
3 & 3 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$6=2 \times 3$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 8 \\
\hline
2 & 4 \\
\hline
2 & 2 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$8=2 \times 2 \times 2$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 12 \\
\hline
2 & 6 \\
\hline
3 & 3 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$12=2 \times 2 \times 3$$
Any multiple of 6 must contain: $3$ ($2$ is included in $2\times2\times2$ below)
Any multiple of 8 must contain: $2 \times 2\times 2$
Requirements for multiples of 12 are already listed ($2\times2$ is included in $2\times2\times2$; $3$ listed for the number $6$)
$$\therefore \text{LCM} = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3 = 24$$

10, 16 and 18
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 10 \\
\hline
5 & 5 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$10=2 \times 5$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 16 \\
\hline
2 & 8 \\
\hline
2 & 4 \\
\hline
2 & 2 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$16=2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$$
$$\begin{array}{r | r}
2 & 18 \\
\hline
3 & 9 \\
\hline
3 & 3 \\
\hline
& 1
\end{array}$$
$$18=2 \times 3 \times 3$$
Any multiple of 10 must contain: $5$ ($2$ is included in $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ below)
Any multiple of 16 must contain: $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$
Any multiple of 18 must contain: $3 \times 3$ ($2$ is included in $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2$ above)
$$\therefore \text{LCM} = 5 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 = 720$$

record.prompt_text: Find the HCF and the LCM of 24 and 32.
record.answer_text:
Step 1: Express each number as a product of prime factors in index form.

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 24 \\
 \hline
 2 & 12 \\
 \hline
 2 & 6 \\
 \hline
 3 & 3 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$24=2^3 \times 3$$

$$\begin{array}{r | r}
 2 & 32 \\
 \hline
 2 & 16 \\
 \hline
 2 & 8 \\
 \hline
 2 & 4 \\
 \hline
 2 & 2 \\
 \hline
 & 1
 \end{array}$$

$$32=2^5$$

Step 2: For the HCF, identify the common prime factors to the lowest index. For the LCM, list all the prime factors to the highest index.

| HCF | LCM |
| --- | --- |
| $2^3$ | $2^5\times3$ |
| $2\times2\times2=8$ | $2\times2\times2\times2\times2\times3=96$ |
| Largest number that can divide into 24 and 32 | Smallest number into which 24 and 32 can divide |
